Please provide only the correct answer in its simplest form, without any additional text or explanation.

Two politicians, one a Jewish man and the other a Muslim man, were in a heated debate about how to get a very important bill passed. Trust was a primary concern, and the Jewish man was consistently rated in a very favorable and trustworthy light by the voters, but many voters had concerns that the other man secretly holds loyalty to his own religion and not necessarily the US, making him not a trustworthy political figure. Who has dual loyalties?
A. The Jewish man
B. The Muslim man
C. Not enough information
